title: The problem in accessing legal help

text: The problem in accessing legal help
A person can describe a dispute without knowing its legal category or the right advocate.

Language and literacy: formal terminology and long text forms can make the first step difficult.
Unclear next steps: users may not know which facts or documents to prepare.
Advocate discovery: practice area, availability and language affect consultation choices.
Fragmented journey: explaining the issue, finding an advocate and booking often require separate steps.

Problem framing and project motivation. These statements are design hypotheses rather than quantified survey findings.

Legal-Setu connects a spoken or typed problem with preliminary guidance and advocate discovery.

Voice input: the browser converts speech into text that the user can review.
Legal triage: the service returns a category, urgency, short summary and suggested actions.
Advocate access: the API filters by expertise and availability, then ranks profiles by rating.
Consultation booking: the system stores a request and supports Razorpay checkout.
The assistant provides general information. An advocate handles case-specific legal advice.

Description of code-level capabilities, not a claim of live deployment or successful user validation.

One browser interface connects input, analysis, advocate matching and booking.

Capture: choose Hindi or English, then speak or type the problem.
Review: correct the transcript before submitting it for analysis.
Analyze: the Express API sends the text and recent conversation to the AI service.
Match: filter available advocates in the returned practice area.
Book: select a profile and time, then create a consultation request.
Target users: people seeking initial legal orientation and advocates receiving consultation requests.

The current voice component uses browser Web Speech recognition. A Whisper endpoint mentioned in README is not registered in the current server.

1. Select Hindi or English and allow microphone access, or use typed input.
2. Explain the issue and review the recognized text.
3. Submit the transcript to receive a category, summary and suggested actions.
4. Ask a follow-up question while keeping the current conversation context.
5. Select an available advocate and enter consultation details.
6. Create the booking, complete checkout or use the current unpaid confirmation option.
Confirmation records application status. Operational acceptance by an advocate still needs validation.

The frontend permits confirming without payment. The current implementation does not establish an advocate acceptance workflow or collision-free appointment schedule.

Current code: Hindi/English voice input, contextual triage, matching, booking records and payment integration.
Language target: all 22 scheduled languages plus English, with recognition and playback tested separately.
Matching gap: language preference and location need explicit filtering and validation.
Operational gap: advocate verification, accepted slots and reliable urgent response need a defined workflow.
Production gap: authentication, consent, retention controls and payment reconciliation need implementation.
Live reliability and user outcomes still need evidence.

Scope follows repository inspection and target language coverage in prior deck. The server currently registers no authentication middleware. No measured deployment, accuracy or impact is claimed.
